title: Corporate web proxy does not send Kerberos authentication for iframe content since Firefox 108.0.1
body: We use a corporate proxy with Kerberos authentication, where content is unavailable without authentication. Since updating Firefox to 108.0.1, pages load normally except for embedded iframe content. Firefox sends authentication for the rest of the page but not for the iframe request, so the proxy refuses the connection; our proxy logs also show that no authentication was sent. This happens consistently on different laptops and virtual machines. Older Firefox versions work, while beta and Nightly are also affected. There were no changes to our corporate proxy. Embedded iframe content should be authenticated through the proxy and load normally.

symptoms_visible: Since Firefox 108.0.1, the main page loads through the Kerberos-authenticated corporate proxy, but embedded iframe content shows that the proxy server is refusing the connection.
The same behavior occurs on different laptops and virtual machines; an older Firefox version loads the iframe correctly.
N0.label: N0 iframe proxy-auth regression reported

symptoms_visible: The iframe still fails to load through the proxy while the rest of the page loads.
N1.label: N1 regression range collected

symptoms_visible: The iframe remains unavailable, and the corporate proxy continues to refuse its request while the surrounding page loads.
N2.label: N2 HTTP log identifies regressing behavior

symptoms_visible: The iframe still shows the proxy refusal, and no setting is available to disable X-Frame-Options on the corporate proxy.
N3.label: N3 proxy response distinguished from site policy

symptoms_visible: In the latest Nightly containing the backout, the page and its iframe load without any issues through the corporate proxy.
N4.label: N4 backout verified in Nightly

symptoms_visible: The verified backout is available for Firefox 109.0.1 and Firefox 110.0b6, restoring authenticated iframe loading in the affected enterprise proxy environment.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Could you run mozregression to determine which Firefox change introduced the problem?
Can you provide the last working and first broken build or the resulting regression range?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran mozregression. It selected the 2022-11-11 Firefox 108.0a1 build at changeset b7164776589657b7d7fd40d32268b2a489eed789, with the pushlog range from df541ee6f62267803ead2b4e966dc2c06a23c58a to b7164776589657b7d7fd40d32268b2a489eed789.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Mozregression shows the problem exists in all tested Firefox builds and instead begins after a corporate proxy configuration change.
The same 2022-11-11 regression range is found, but the test was run on another affected laptop.

edges.comment: Comment 1-2: the reporter ran mozregression and supplied the precise first-bad build, changeset, and pushlog range.

question_patterns: Could you record an HTTP log while reproducing the iframe failure?
Please send a Firefox networking log privately because it may contain sensitive information.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I recorded the HTTP log and sent the file by email to participant9.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The log shows Firefox sends Kerberos credentials on the iframe request and the authenticated origin server rejects them.

edges.comment: Comments 3-9: the private HTTP log contained an X-Frame-Options: deny response. Engineers correlated the log and regression range with bug 1629307.

question_patterns: Is the X-Frame-Options: deny header added by the corporate proxy or by the original website?
Can you confirm where the X-Frame-Options response seen in the log comes from?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The X-Frame-Options: deny response is from the corporate proxy after Firefox fails to send Kerberos authentication; the proxy then answers with NTLM Negotiate as a fallback. We do not manipulate the website's content through the proxy.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The original website itself always sends X-Frame-Options: deny, including when accessed without the corporate proxy.
The proxy uses a different product version on one test laptop, but the response and Firefox behavior are unchanged.

question_patterns: Does the proxy add or alter security headers on successfully authenticated website content?
Is the corporate proxy modifying the site's response content?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. We only scan for malicious content and do not manipulate the website content.

question_patterns: Can you temporarily disable the proxy's X-Frame-Options behavior to test it as a workaround?
Is there a proxy setting available to remove X-Frame-Options?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found no option to disable X-Frame-Options.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is an option, but toggling it does not restore Kerberos authentication for the iframe.

edges.comment: Comments 9-11: this config/source probe ruled out treating the header as an origin CSP policy or as a configurable proxy content modification. The proxy emitted it as part of the unauthenticated fallback response.

question_patterns: Can you test the latest Nightly containing the backout of bug 1629307?
Please verify whether today's Nightly restores iframe loading through the Kerberos proxy.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested today's Nightly and can confirm that the issue is resolved. The page and its iframe now load without any issues again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Nightly containing the backout still fails to authenticate the iframe request in exactly the same way.
The iframe works in the backout Nightly on one laptop, and the other affected machines have not yet been retested.

edges.comment: Comments 19-24: after the backout landed on central, the reporter tested the next Nightly and explicitly confirmed that the page loaded normally.

solution.intent: Back out bug 1629307, which incorrectly suppressed proxy authentication for iframe requests after interpreting the proxy's unauthenticated X-Frame-Options response as proof that the iframe could not load, then uplift the verified backout to supported beta and release branches.
solution.concrete_example: Back out the iframe X-Frame-Options authentication-suppression change from bug 1629307. After the reporter verifies the backout in Nightly, uplift it to Firefox 110.0b6 and Firefox 109.0.1 so Kerberos proxy authentication is again attempted for the iframe request.

edges.comment: Comments 12-29: bug 1629307 was backed out, the reporter verified the fix in Nightly, and the backout was approved and landed for Firefox 110.0b6 and 109.0.1.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the true root cause: bug 1629307 suppressed authentication for iframe requests when an X-Frame-Options/CSP check suggested the frame could not load; in this environment, the X-Frame-Options: deny response came from the corporate proxy only after Kerberos authentication was absent, causing Firefox to suppress the authentication needed to escape that response.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: the Firefox-only regression and unchanged proxy, the mozregression range, the private HTTP log containing X-Frame-Options: deny, and the reporter's explanation that this was the proxy's unauthenticated fallback response rather than an origin policy.

Must not settle on disabling X-Frame-Options or changing the corporate proxy as the resolution: the reporter found no such option, the proxy does not manipulate authenticated site content, and the regression was fixed by backing out Firefox bug 1629307.
Must propose or describe backing out the regressing bug 1629307 and carrying the backout to the affected release channels.
Must require the reporter's successful test of a Nightly containing the backout before declaring the issue resolved, and should include the Firefox 110.0b6 and 109.0.1 rollout.

persona_hint.experience_level: Enterprise IT reporter with practical knowledge of corporate Kerberos proxy behavior and access to proxy logs; capable of running mozregression, collecting a sensitive Firefox HTTP log, and testing Nightly builds.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, concise, and cooperative. Provides concrete technical results when asked, explains the enterprise proxy behavior from operational knowledge, and seeks confirmation about when a landed fix is available to test.
